fullDescription: A settings and preferences screen designed as a classic 1 bit desktop operating system. A dithered black and white checkerboard desktop sits inside a warm near black bezel, one window carries a striped title bar with a square close box, and a two pane shell splits a category rail from the settings list. Only that pane scrolls, so the page itself never moves and the screen reads as software rather than a web page. Every control is period correct: square checkboxes with a hand drawn tick, radio pairs, a stepper with square arrow boxes, a slider with a square handle, a triangle dropdown and an inset text field, plus a default button marked by a doubled border instead of a colour fill. Strictly monochrome apart from two accent dots. Use it for developer tools, indie software, archives, documentation and any product UI that should feel operated rather than browsed.
prompt:
## Resumo
A settings/preferences application screen built as a classic bitmap desktop operating system rather than a webpage wearing retro decoration. The full 100vh viewport is wrapped in a warm near-black #282725 bezel with 8px rounded outer corners. A fixed white menu bar with a 1px black border carries a small line-art glyph, the menus File, Edit, View and Special in a bitmap system face, and three 14px status dots at far right in #f37725, #3685c5 and black. The desktop below is a crisp 1-bit 50% dithered checkerboard of pure black on white from a repeating 4px CSS pattern, never a grey fill and never a gradient. One centred preferences window at ~62% width sits on it in pure #ffffff with a 1px pure-black border and 8px radius; its title bar is six horizontal 1px black rules running edge to edge, interrupted by a square close box at the left and a centred title. A second smaller window peeks from behind, axis-aligned and offset down-right ~24px, with an unstriped inactive bar. Inside, a two-pane shell: a left rail of seven category rows (General, Appearance, Sound, Network, Storage, Sharing, Startup), each a 1px line-art icon above a caption, with the active row inverted to white-on-black; and a right pane that is the ONLY scrolling region, carrying a real dithered scrollbar (checkerboard trough, square 1px-bordered arrow boxes top and bottom, plain white thumb). Settings rows are separated by full-width 1px black rules and pair a label with a period-correct control: a square 4px checkbox with a hand-drawn tick, a classic radio pair, a stepper with two square arrow boxes, a slider with a 1px track and a square handle, a dropdown with a small solid triangle, and a text field with a 1px inset border. A bottom bar inside the window holds a disclosure caption at left and Revert plus Save at right, the default marked by a doubled 2px border rather than a fill. Outside the window, a right-edge rail of line-art desktop icons under 1px-bordered caption labels. Strictly monochrome apart from the two accent hues. No hero, no marketing headline, no CTA, no gradient, no shadow, no rounded cards.

## Estilo Visual
Design a monochrome 1-bit desktop-OS application screen. Wrap the full 100vh viewport in a warm near-black #282725 bezel with 8px rounded outer corners. Fill the desktop with a crisp 1-bit 50% dithered checkerboard of pure black on white from a repeating 4px CSS background pattern, never a grey fill or gradient. Make every surface pure #ffffff with 1px pure-black borders and no shadow, blur or elevation. Use 8px radius on window chrome, 4px on controls, 0px everywhere else. Set all chrome in Chicago, ChiKareGo, Monaco, Courier New, monospace at ~0.02em tracking, and all content in Verdana, Geneva, sans-serif at 15px/400 with 1.5 line-height and 20px/700 section heads. Allow exactly two hues, #f37725 and #3685c5, confined to status dots and links. No modern sans, no emoji, no gradients, no soft grey UI, no rounded cards, no hero.

## Layout e Estrutura

### Bezel, menu bar and desktop
Wrap the viewport in a warm near-black #282725 frame roughly 16px thick with 8px rounded outer corners. Inside it, a fixed white menu bar with a 1px black border carrying a small line-art glyph at far left, the menus File, Edit, View and Special in the bitmap face, and three 14px dots at far right in #f37725, #3685c5 and black. Below, the desktop is a repeating 4px 1-bit dithered checkerboard of pure black on white, crisp and unsmoothed.

### Preferences window and title bar
A centred white window at about 62% width with a 1px pure-black border and 8px radius. Its title bar is six horizontal 1px black rules running edge to edge, interrupted at the left by a small square close box and at the centre by the window title in the bitmap face. Place a second smaller window peeking behind it, axis-aligned, offset down-right about 24px, with a plain unstriped inactive title bar.

### Two-pane shell with category rail
Split the window interior into a narrow left category rail and a wide right pane, divided by a 1px black rule. The rail lists seven rows — General, Appearance, Sound, Network, Storage, Sharing, Startup — each a simple 1px line-art icon above a caption in the bitmap face. The active row inverts to white-on-black across the full rail width. Give every row an icon; a rail with some rows iconless reads as unfinished.

### Settings rows and controls
Fill the right pane with settings rows separated by full-width 1px black rules, each pairing a label with a period-correct control: a square 4px checkbox with a hand-drawn tick, a classic radio pair, a stepper with two small square arrow boxes, a slider with a 1px track and a square handle, a dropdown with a small solid triangle, and a text field with a 1px inset border. Write real, specific setting labels for the product; never lorem, never placeholder.

### Dithered scrollbar
Give the right pane the only scrollbar on the screen: a 1-bit checkerboard trough, square 1px-bordered arrow boxes at top and bottom carrying small solid triangles, and a plain white 1px-bordered thumb. No rounded ends, no translucency, no auto-hide.

### Window bottom bar and icon rail
Close the window with a bottom bar: a small disclosure caption at left and two 4px-radius buttons at right, where the default action is marked by a doubled 2px border rather than a colour fill. Outside the window, down the right edge of the desktop, stack line-art icons for a hard drive, a folder and a document, each under a small white caption label box with a 1px black border. Use only generic labels; never a real product or platform name.

## Componentes Especiais de UI

### Inverted active rail row — Selection state carried by inversion instead of colour.
Mark the selected category by inverting the entire rail row to white-on-black across its full width, icon included. No accent fill, no left border, no bold weight change. In a monochrome system inversion is the strongest available emphasis, which is why it is reserved for the single selected item.

### Period-correct control set — The reason an OS metaphor pays off on an app screen rather than a landing page.
Build the form controls to pre-colour OS conventions: a square 4px checkbox with a hand-drawn tick, a classic radio circle with a solid centre dot, a numeric stepper with two stacked square arrow boxes, a slider with a 1px track and a square handle, a dropdown ending in a small solid triangle, and a text field with a 1px inset border. Every control is 1px black on white with no fill, no shadow and no rounded pill shapes.

### Doubled-border default button — The default action marked without colour.
In a button pair, distinguish the default action with a doubled 2px border around the button rather than a filled background, matching pre-colour OS conventions. The secondary button keeps a single 1px border. Never use a coloured fill to mark the default in this system.

### Window-scoped scrolling — The conceit that makes it an OS rather than a page.
Constrain the entire composition to 100vh so the page itself never scrolls, and make a single interior pane the only scrolling region, with its own visible scrollbar. If the whole screen scrolls, the metaphor collapses into a themed webpage.

style.description: Monochrome 1-bit retro-computing skeuomorphism applied to a real application screen. The ground is a dithered pattern rather than a colour; every surface is pure white with 1px pure-black borders and zero elevation. Radius is a small specific vocabulary — 8px window chrome, 4px controls, 0px everything else. Type splits by role: a bitmap system face for all chrome and a normal body face for content, which is what separates a genuine interface metaphor from a costume. Exactly two hues exist and they appear only as status dots and links.

layout_and_structure.description: A single non-scrolling screen: bezel > menu bar > dithered desktop > one centred preferences window with a two-pane interior, plus a peeking second window and a right-edge icon rail. The right settings pane is the only scrolling region. On narrow screens the left category rail becomes a horizontal scrolling strip above the pane and the window goes full-bleed, while the bezel and dithered ground are preserved.
